content: To begin, load the Patient Information Page template. This template has been specifically designed to ensure maximum user-friendliness. All coding should adhere to this format. Replace the placeholder text Type page name here in the code with the name of the condition you are addressing. Similarly, whenever the word (condition) appears, substitute it with the specific name of the condition. Important Notes: 1. If your patient information page is derived from a mature chapter, include the coding for the expanded navigation template. 2. Check the WikiDoc condition main page to copy the appropriate InfoBox links. The InfoBox is the code that appears at the top of the condition's main page and provides additional resources such as ICD-10, ICD-9, ICD-0, OMIM, MedlinePlus, eMedicine Subj, eMedicine Topic, MeSH Name, etc. If no such code exists on the condition's main page, do not add one. Coding Guidelines: Remove the Editor Join template. The SI and SIB templates should only be included if no expanded navigation template exists. There should never be both an SI/SIB template and an expanded navigation template on the same page. Proper capitalization is critical in WikiDoc coding. For example, Category: Page name here must follow the correct format. Patient Information Page Content: Search the National Library of Medicine and other government sites to ensure the patient page is comprehensive. The goal of the page is to provide patient-oriented information, generally addressing the background, diagnosis, and treatment of the condition. The content should be written at an 8th-grade reading level and avoid overly technical language. Appropriate Content Sections: 1. Overview 2. What are the symptoms of the condition? 3. What causes the condition? 4. Who is at the highest risk? 5. When to seek urgent medical care? 6. Diagnosis 7. Treatment options 8. Where to find medical care for the condition? 9. Directions to hospitals treating the condition 10. What to expect (Outlook/Prognosis)? 11. Possible complications 12. Sources Additional Instructions: Include a link back to the physician page of WikiDoc at the top of the page. Always place an Editor-In-Chief code at the top of the page. Never copy content directly from a source without verifying copyright. Content should not be directly copied from PubMed articles, copyrighted encyclopedias, or similar sources. Categorization of the Patient Information Page: Place the page in the Category: Patient information. If the condition pertains to a specific system, code a category for the system involved. For example, leukemia would fall under Hematology as it involves the circulatory system. All pages should be designated as Category: Overview complete once an overview statement is included. Patient information pages should also include additional applicable categories such as Drug, Disease state, Surgery, etc.
